title: Control Flow, Functions aur Arrays
objectives: Typed functions, default values aur named arguments use karna
prerequisites: PHP Basics: Variables, Data Types aur Operators (m01-l01)

sections.heading: Decisions: if aur match
sections.body: Program ko decision lene ke liye `if` use hota hai. Jab ek value ke kai options ho, to `match` zyada saaf hota hai (PHP 8.0+). `match` strict comparison (`===`) karta hai aur value return karta hai.

code.code:
<?php

$stock = 4;

if ($stock > 10) {
    echo 'Plenty';
} elseif ($stock > 0) {
    echo 'Low stock';
} else {
    echo 'Out of stock';
}

$status = 'shipped';

$message = match ($status) {
    'pending'   => 'Order process ho raha hai',
    'shipped'   => 'Order bhej diya gaya',
    'delivered' => 'Order mil gaya',
    default     => 'Unknown status',
};

echo $message;

explain: `match` ek value return karta hai, isliye seedha `$message` mein store ho gaya.
Agar koi arm match na kare aur `default` na ho, to `UnhandledMatchError` aata hai.

sections.heading: Real-world example: Shopping cart
sections.body: Cart ek array hai, jisme har item ek chhota array hai (name, price, qty). Total nikalne ke liye `foreach` se har item par loop chalate hain.

sections.heading: Functions
sections.body: Function ek reusable code block hai. Parameters aur return ka type likhna achhi aadat hai. PHP 8 mein **named arguments** se order ki chinta nahi rehti.

code.code:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

function lineTotal(int $price, int $qty = 1): int
{
    return $price * $qty;
}

echo lineTotal(799, 2);          // 1598
echo lineTotal(qty: 3, price: 100); // 300

$gst = fn (int $amount): float => $amount * 0.18;

echo $gst(1000); // 180

explain: `int $qty = 1` – default value; argument na do to 1 lagega.
`fn (...) => ...` – arrow function, ek line ka chhota function. Bahar ke variables apne aap mil jaate hain.

sections.heading: Array functions
sections.body: Arrays par kaam karne ke liye built-in functions hain. Laravel mein inka bada version **Collections** hai (aage ke modules mein).

code.code:
<?php

$prices = [799, 1499, 250];

$withGst   = array_map(fn ($p) => $p * 1.18, $prices);
$expensive = array_filter($prices, fn ($p) => $p > 500);

echo array_sum($prices); // 2548
echo count($prices);     // 3

print_r($expensive);     // [0 => 799, 1 => 1499]

explain: `array_map` – har element par function chalata hai, naya array deta hai.
`array_filter` – sirf wahi elements rakhta hai jinke liye function `true` de. Original keys bani rehti hain.

callout.text: Laravel mein `collect($prices)->map(...)->filter(...)` likhte hain. Concept yahi hai, bas syntax aur saaf hota hai.

versionDiff.heading: Version notes
versionDiff.intro: Control flow, functions aur arrays ka behaviour teeno Laravel versions mein same hai (sab PHP 8.2+ par chalte hain).

items.11: `match`, named arguments, arrow functions sab available hain (PHP 8.2+).

errors.cause: Array mein woh key nahi hai jo tum padh rahe ho.
errors.fix: Key ka spelling dekho, ya `$item['qty'] ?? 1` se default do.

errors.error: TypeError: lineTotal(): Argument #1 ($price) must be of type int, string given
errors.fix: Int pass karo ya `(int) $value` se cast karo.

errors.cause: Same naam ka function do baar define hua (aksar file do baar include hone se).
errors.fix: Function ek hi jagah define karo, aur `require_once` use karo.

debug.body: Array ko readable form mein dekhne ke liye `print_r()` ko `<pre>` ke saath use karo (browser mein), ya terminal mein seedha `print_r()`/`var_dump()`.

tasks: Ek `$marks` array banao (5 numbers) aur average nikalo
`array_filter` se 40 se kam marks wale subjects nikalo

quiz.q: `match` kis type ki comparison karta hai?
quiz.why: `match` strict comparison karta hai aur value return karta hai.

options: Condition pass karne wale elements rakhta hai
quiz.why: `array_filter` callback ke `true` dene par hi element rakhta hai.

quiz.q: Named argument ka example kaunsa hai?
quiz.why: Named arguments `naam: value` format mein likhte hain.

interview.a: `match` strict comparison karta hai, value return karta hai, fall-through nahi hota aur match na ho to `UnhandledMatchError` deta hai.
`fn ($x) => expression` – ek expression wala chhota function jo parent scope ke variables automatically capture karta hai.

interview.q: Indexed aur associative array mein farak?
interview.a: Indexed array mein keys numbers (0, 1, 2) hoti hain. Associative mein keys naam hote hain (`'name' => 'Mouse'`).

interview.q: `array_map` aur `foreach` mein kab kya use karein?
interview.a: Jab har element ko transform karke naya array chahiye to `array_map`. Jab side effects ya complex logic ho to `foreach`.
Order ki chinta nahi rehti, aur code padhne mein saaf hota hai, khaaskar jab bahut optional parameters hon.

summary: `if` aur `match` se decisions lete hain; `match` strict hai.
Typed functions, default values aur named arguments code ko saaf banate hain.
`array_map`, `array_filter`, `array_sum` arrays ke liye kaam ke tools hain.
Laravel Collections inhi ideas par bane hain.
